checks.note: restoreCoachPriceAndVoidDowngrade / restorePlayerPriceAndVoidDowngrade (reached from the newRank == currentRank branch of changeCoachTier/changePlayerTier) move the Stripe price back up via updateStripePrice with chargeNow=false and void the pending change without any check of what the last renewal invoice billed; the changeCoachTier javadoc itself confirms Stripe renews before the daily applyPendingChanges run, so the post-renewal window exists and the user keeps the higher local tier having paid the downgraded renewal price.

assertCanSubscribe runs on an unlocked read and createPaidStripeSubscription uses a per-attempt key ("sub-create-" + UUID.randomUUID()), so concurrent subscribes each create and synchronously pay a Stripe subscription (error_if_incomplete per the class javadoc); the persist loser (isOtherLiveSubscription in persistCoachSubscription/persistPlayerSubscription) is cancelled via cancelStripeSubscriptionQuietly → cancelSubscriptionImmediately, and Stripe's immediate cancel never auto-refunds — no Refund/credit call exists anywhere in this file for the DUPLICATE path.

The race window and deliberate revoke are confirmed in the shown code — GraceTarget.matches returns true on an unchanged non-null stripeSubscriptionId regardless of status ("even if an invoice.paid raced in"), and the Stripe cancel in cancelAtStripeForGrace runs after the phase-1 lock is released. But the described consequence (charged retry kept, no refund) depends on StripeClient.cancelSubscriptionImmediately's retrieve-then-cancel/refund behavior, which is not in the provided hunks.

The race window is real: applyCoachChange/applyPlayerChange commit phase 1 (releasing the lock) before syncStripePriceForChange calls stripeClient.updateSubscriptionTier unconditionally, and phase 2's pendingCoachChange/stripeSubscriptionId filter only blocks the local apply, so a concurrent upgrade in the gap leaves Stripe at the downgrade price. But the claimed persistence of the drift depends on reconcileStripeSubscriptions(), which is referenced in reconcileMarketplaceTiers's javadoc as the "Stripe → payment side" yet whose body is not in the diff — if it compares Stripe item prices to stored tiers it would correct the drift, and that cannot be confirmed or refuted here.

handleInvoicePaid guards only with isStaleEvent and RECOVERABLE_ON_PAYMENT, then sets ACTIVE and clears pastDueSince without checking billing_reason or Stripe's subscription status; Stripe emits invoice.paid per invoice (including non-latest invoices of an unpaid subscription, which don't reactivate it), and the staleness check passes since the payment event is newer than lastStripeEventAt.

matches.note: R4 identifies the same defect: grace sweep filters PAST_DUE only, so UNPAID/PAUSED rows are never cancelled at Stripe (which keeps invoicing) and never closed locally, matching F1's mechanism and consequence.
